description: Use an open tub of ricotta in five practical savoury dinner routes: baked tray, skillet, filling, quick sauce, or crisp fritters.
h1: What to Make With Ricotta: 5 Savory Dinner Routes for a Tub in the Fridge
intro: A tub of ricotta can carry a whole dinner. Its mild flavour works with sharp greens, tomatoes, lemon, beans, pasta, potatoes, and crisp breadcrumbs. Start by deciding what you want from tonight: a soft baked centre, a quick skillet meal, something filled, a creamy sauce, or a crisp-edged fritter.
Use this guide as a route selector. Each route gives ricotta a different job, so you can choose from the ingredients and equipment already within reach.

sections.heading: Choose the route before you choose the recipe

rows: An oven and vegetables that benefit from roasting

paragraphs_after: A small tub suits sauce, skillet, or fritter routes. Use more generous spoonfuls for baking and stuffing.

sections.heading: 1. Build a baked ricotta tray
paragraphs: Choose this route when you have an oven, a vegetable that can roast, and enough time to let the edges turn golden.
**Start with:**
**How to assemble it**
Serve it with bread, a grain, or a salad. Leftover beans turn it into a more substantial tray with very little extra work.
list: sliced aubergine, courgette, mushrooms, peppers, tomatoes, or cooked greens;
something sharp: lemon zest, grated hard cheese, capers, chilli, or herbs;
breadcrumbs or torn bread for the top.
steps: Roast or sauté the vegetables until they have taken on some colour.
Stir ricotta with lemon zest, salt, pepper, herbs, and a little grated cheese if you have it.
Layer the vegetables and ricotta in a shallow dish.
Cover with breadcrumbs, oil, and a little more cheese.
Bake until hot through and crisp on top.

sections.heading: 2. Finish a quick skillet with ricotta
paragraphs: Choose this route for a weeknight pan of vegetables, beans, greens, or gnocchi. Ricotta goes in at the end, where it adds soft pockets and takes the edge off a spicy or tomato-rich base.
**Good starting points:**

Cook the base first. Add a little water, stock, or pasta water if the pan needs loosening. Spoon ricotta over the top, cover briefly, then finish with lemon, black pepper, herbs, or a drizzle of olive oil.
Keep the ricotta in visible spoonfuls. Each serving gets a creamy point of contrast while the pan stays light.
list: white beans with kale or spinach;
leftover roasted vegetables warmed with garlic and chilli.

sections.heading: 3. Use ricotta as a seasoned filling
paragraphs: Choose this route when you have something to fill: large pasta shells, cannelloni, tortillas, pitta, baked potatoes, mushrooms, or halved peppers.
Mix ricotta with one strong flavour direction:
paragraphs_after: Fill the chosen base, add a small amount of sauce or vegetables around it, and bake or pan-warm until the centre is hot. The filling works best when one element is bright or savoury enough to lead the flavour.

sections.heading: 4. Turn ricotta into a quick dinner sauce
paragraphs: Ricotta makes a fast sauce for pasta, gnocchi, beans, or roasted vegetables. It needs a little warm liquid and a bright finishing ingredient to become smooth and lively.
For two portions, combine in a bowl:
Toss with hot pasta or gnocchi until the sauce coats everything. Fold in peas, spinach, roasted vegetables, beans, or shredded chicken if you have them.
For a tomato version, warm tomato sauce first, then add the ricotta in spoonfuls at the end. The separate creamy pockets make a simple sauce feel more generous.
list: a splash of pasta water, stock, or hot water;
lemon zest or a squeeze of lemon;
grated cheese, herbs, chilli, or chopped olives if available.

sections.heading: 5. Make crisp ricotta fritters
paragraphs: This route is useful when you have a small amount of ricotta plus cooked potato, courgette, greens, grains, or vegetables that need a new shape.

Mix ricotta with the cooked ingredient, an egg if you use eggs, a little flour or breadcrumbs, and a strong seasoning such as herbs, lemon, chilli, garlic, or grated cheese. Form small patties and cook in a lightly oiled pan until both sides are browned.
Serve fritters with:
Aim for a mixture that holds together when pressed. If it feels loose, add breadcrumbs a spoonful at a time.
list: a spoonful of yoghurt or a sharp green sauce;
bread and a handful of leaves.
